note: First pass: loader_ctx initialized with p_code_compiled=NULL, so all emit functions only increment code_compiled_size to compute required buffer size.
After first pass, code_compiled_size holds the total bytes needed. Reinit resets p_code_compiled to the start of the allocated buffer for the second pass.

In second pass, wasm_loader_emit_ptr writes 8 bytes (sizeof(void*)) via STORE_PTR without any bounds check against p_code_compiled_end. If the second pass emits more bytes than the first pass computed, this write overflows the heap buffer.

preserve_referenced_local emits EXT_OP_COPY_STACK_TOP plus operands. In the first pass, preserved_local_offset is INT16_MAX (a sentinel); in the second pass it holds the actual offset. The size of emitted code depends on this value, and if the branch taken differs between passes, the second pass can emit more bytes than the first pass accounted for.

wasm_loader_emit_backspace reduces the emitted code size. If the first pass calls backspace but the second pass does not (or vice versa), the size computation diverges between passes, causing the second pass to write past the allocated buffer.

Second pass begins. The buffer was allocated based on code_compiled_size from the first pass. Any divergence in emission size between passes leads to a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 in wasm_loader_emit_ptr during the second pass.

The heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 occurs here: STORE_PTR writes 8 bytes past the end of the allocated code buffer because the second pass emitted more code than the first pass computed. The root cause is a size-mismatch between the two passes in preserve_referenced_local or related label/backspace logic.
